newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares slide, no pick-up seen this month.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares slide, no pick-up seen this month.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell 1.73 percent on Tuesday and traders said an upswing could only be expected after April when banks open first custodian accounts for international investors.
"The return of foreign investors is expected to bring expectations of better liquidity and higher prices even if volumes do not increase significantly as soon as in April," one trader said.

The Bank of Slovenia five weeks ago blocked foreign buying by saying international investors have to open custodian accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in Slovenian shares. Since then the index has fallen 19.2 percent.
* The SBI index fell 23.56 points to 1,338.26.
* Issue A of drug company Lek was most actively traded, easing 0.26 percent to 26,590 tolars on volume of 783 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
